suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-30 adds this relationship only as a bounded migraine-variant association. Alice in Wonderland syndrome is described in contemporary clinical literature as a migraine variant and precursor occurring predominantly in pediatric populations, frequently accompanied by personal or family history of migraine, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish a migraine diagnosis in every person or determine an individual's headache course. Require independently documented AIWS episodes with characteristic visual distortions, documented migraine headache meeting ICHD criteria compatible in chronology, and specialist neurologic review. Preserve epilepsy, infectious and autoimmune encephalitis, psychotropic and other medication effects, cerebrovascular disease, and other competing causes of metamorphopsia and distortory perception.

sourceReferences.citation: Bandatmakur ASM, Sivaswamy L. Migraine Variants and Precursors in Childhood: Clinical Features, Diagnostic Challenges, and Management Approaches. Pediatr Ann. 2026;55(5):e195-e200. PMID 42065956. doi:10.3928/19382359-20260304-02.
sourceReferences.note: Contemporary review classifying Alice in Wonderland syndrome among pediatric migraine variants and precursors, highlighting paroxysmal phenomenology and frequent migraine family history. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 42065956; AIWS classified within pediatric migraine-variant spectrum

nexusClaim.associationBasis: AIWS is described within the migraine-variant spectrum with frequent migraine association, but the classification evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both syndromes, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: AIWS is treated clinically as a migraine variant, with hypothesized shared cortical spreading and visual-network mechanisms, but the precise shared mechanism must be established from the individual's headache history, perimorphic episode documentation, and specialist neurologic evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. AIWS appears within the migraine-variant and precursor spectrum in clinical review literature, but that classification does not establish that AIWS caused or aggravated migraine in every individual; both diagnoses, chronology, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented AIWS episodes and ICHD-defined migraine; chronology; epilepsy, encephalitis, medication, and cerebrovascular alternatives; specialist neurologic assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Epilepsy or structural brain disease causing distortory perceptual episodes
Psychotropic or other medication effects, and primary psychiatric perceptual disturbance
